verdict.rationale: Increase's docs show rich transactional metadata: unique per-counterparty Account Numbers for auto-reconciliation, ACH Addenda access, real-time network events/webhooks tracking submission-acknowledgment-return status, Entity objects as stable counterparty identifiers, and routing-number reachability checks — all reinforced by customer case studies (Ramp using per-user accounts and low-level rail access, fund-admin reconciling capital calls via unique account numbers). Community comments corroborate that Increase deliberately avoids abstracting away rail-specific detail, giving developers direct access to underlying payment mechanics rather than a leaky abstraction. Missing for 10: independent hands-on confirmation of full counterparty-metadata schema depth and enrichment coverage across less-common rails (e.g., check images, card network data) beyond marketing/docs claims.
